ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 to L561-59 and R561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), as amended by Ordonnance n°2020-115 and Décret n°2020-118 of 12 February 2020; Loi n°2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Articles L123-11, L123-12 and R123-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code on the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE), governed by Décret n°2016-1783 of 16 December 2016, as amended; transposition of Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD); RBE integrated into the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) effective 1 January 2023.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the holder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization) plus certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille for signature legalization; certified French translation; must state precise corporate name and purpose

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank of the shareholder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Apostille (or consular path); French translation; also needed for bank account opening on SWIFT/LC rails

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons under FATF Recommendation 12 and Articles L561-10 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier. Systematic screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014), the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the French Treasury (DG Trésor) asset-freeze list, the OFAC SDN List for all USD-denominated SWIFT wires and letters of credit, plus adverse-media and negative-news checks. UBO declaration verification against the RBE in the RNE, with obligations for any change in excess of 25% ownership or control. Legal counsel and the incorporation agent must document the risk rating (High_Risk_Special_License) and customer due diligence file under Article L561-5 CMF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique de l'INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) for submission of the incorporation file; name availability and conflict search through Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr) and the Registre National des Entreprises (registre-national-entreprises.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in the statutes in Latin script; any foreign-language name must be transliterated into Latin characters and appended with the legal-form suffix SAS. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing French or EU trademark or an RCS-registered company name, and must not mislead the public regarding the company's regulated activities.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France / national / mondial when implying state affiliation or unfounded geographic scope
clinique / hospitalier / médical where implying official health approval without the relevant licence
CE / ANSM / biocompatible / stérile where implying a conformity certificate not yet held
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a blocking name-reservation system; a name search result is indicative for 30 days and is formally protected only upon RCS registration. Upon a rejection, the applicant must receive the registrar's written reason under Article L123-4-1 of the Commercial Code; the applicant may cure the defect by re-filing with up to three new variants via the Guichet unique. If the registrar's refusal is contested (e.g., erroneous conflict flag or disproportionate refusal), the applicant may apply to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce in référé within 15 days of the refusal date, or file an administrative claim before the competent civil court; trademark-based refusals are handled by opposition proceedings before the INPI within 2 months of registration publication.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted for an SAS for up to 5 years under Articles L123-11-1 and L123-11-2 of the Commercial Code, using an approved domiciliation company or law firm address. However, the manufacture of Class III intraocular lenses under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) and ISO 13485 requires a physical operational facility subject to notified-body audits and ANSM inspections; a virtual office alone is insufficient commercial substance for ANSM registration, EU customs clearances, and the High_Risk_Special_License banking tier, and will trigger enhanced AML/KYC scrutiny by ACPR/Tracfin.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — approximately 85% likelihood of announced or unannounced physical inspection by the notifying authority (ANSM), the designated notified body (e.g., GMED, TÜV SÜD, BSI), or judicial police within the first 12-24 months of operation; failure to maintain a genuine physical seat and production facility will result in denial or revocation of the MDR certificate and RCS deregistration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS) and Decree No. 2007-431 on commercial formalities
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the National Formalities Portal (Guichet Unique)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and M0 form (or online declaration)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SAS; however, at least 50% of the subscribed capital must be paid up at incorporation, with the remainder payable within 5 years. Capital must be deposited in a French bank account (escrow) before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders of the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) hereby subscribe to the share capital of €[amount] as set forth in the Articles of Association, and the registered office of the company shall be established at [address]. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as President of the SAS, with full powers to represent the company in all dealings with third parties, and that [Name] is appointed as General Manager, if applicable. The President is hereby authorized to complete all incorporation formalities, including the deposit of capital, publication of legal notice, and filing with the Commercial Registry. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional unless real estate contribution) or legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts (Articles of Association) in French, including corporate name, registered office address, share capital, share classes, governance rules, and the appointment of the President. If a notary is used, execute the deed before a notary; otherwise, sign privately. Ensure all shareholders sign and initial each page.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office (lease or ownership document)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the articles, amend the relevant clauses and resubmit with a cover letter explaining the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital in a French Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the company's name and deposit at least 50% of the subscribed capital. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) from the bank, which is required for registration.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays, provide additional KYC documents or choose an alternative bank. The certificate must be issued within 8 days of deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of Legal Notice in a Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a legal notice (avis de constitution) in an authorized legal gazette, containing the company name, legal form (SAS), capital amount, registered office address, purpose, and the identity of the President. Obtain a copy of the publication (attestation de parution).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is rejected due to incomplete information, correct the notice and republish. Ensure the notice appears within 7 days of the deposit of capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Incorporation File with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique (online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation file electronically through the Guichet Unique, including the M0 form, signed Statuts, certificate of capital deposit, proof of legal publication, and proof of registered office. Pay the filing fee online. The registry will review and issue the K-bis extract upon approval.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office (lease or utility bill)
Identity documents of the President and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is incomplete or contains errors, the registry will issue a query (demande de régularisation). Correct the deficiencies within 15 days and resubmit. If the issue persists, seek legal counsel to amend the articles or provide additional documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain K-bis Extract and Register for Social and Tax Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and INSEE (National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the registry issues the K-bis extract (official proof of incorporation) and assigns the SIREN and SIRET numbers. The company is automatically registered with the tax authorities and social security (URSSAF) via the Guichet Unique. Verify the K-bis details and retain for licensing and banking purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis contains errors, request a correction from the registry within 30 days. If SIREN/SIRET numbers are not received, contact INSEE directly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agence Nationale de Sécurité du Médicament et des Produits de Santé (ANSM)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manufacturing Authorization for Medical Devices (Autorisation de fabrication de dispositifs médicaux)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecological Transition – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Déclaration) under ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) for low-impact manufacturing; may require Authorization (Autorisation) if production capacity exceeds thresholds or if hazardous chemicals are used.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French environmental regulations (Code de l'environnement): wastewater discharge limits (pH 6-9, COD < 125 mg/L, BOD5 < 25 mg/L), VOC emissions < 20 mg/m³, and hazardous waste handling per ICPE requirements. Must submit a compliance dossier and obtain a prefectural order.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire department (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours – SDIS), structural load inspection by a certified engineer, and workplace occupational health and safety clearance from the Labor Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail) prior to commencement of operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), through the impots.gouv.fr business tax portal and the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The INPI portal transmits incorporation and amendment data to the competent tax office, which administers corporate income tax, VAT, payroll taxes, and related registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS must be registered through the INPI Guichet unique before commencing business. The registry process generates the SIREN number for the legal entity and the SIRET number for each establishment; these identifiers are recorded in the Registre national des entreprises and generally appear on the Kbis extract. The competent Service des impôts des entreprises opens the tax file and assigns the French intra-Community VAT identification number, normally in the format FR plus a two-digit control key and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment must apply to the non-resident tax service or the competent DGFiP service for a French VAT number where French VAT registration is required. The application normally requires constitutional documents, proof of legal existence, evidence of economic activity, identification of directors and beneficial owners, French establishment details where applicable, bank details, and a description of taxable transactions. The entity must notify DGFiP of changes to registered activities, establishments, directors, beneficial owners, and VAT status. A VAT number must be validated through the VIES system for intra-Community transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) by default. A qualifying SAS may elect for the partnership-style income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu) for a maximum period of five financial years, subject to statutory conditions, including eligibility based on age, ownership, employee headcount, turnover or balance-sheet limits, and qualifying operating activity. The election requires notification to the tax administration within the statutory time limit and is generally irrevocable after the applicable period. France does not provide a general United States-style check-the-box election. French tax classification follows the legal form and specific statutory elections. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework may deny deductions or impose inclusion outcomes but do not constitute a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), supplemented by customs duties and excise rules for imports and exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France applies a VAT franchise regime rather than a single universal registration threshold. The principal annual domestic turnover thresholds are EUR 85,000 for goods, accommodation, and certain comparable activities, with an increased threshold of EUR 93,500, and EUR 37,500 for services and professional activities, with an increased threshold of EUR 41,250. Threshold application depends on the nature of supplies and the applicable tax year. A business may voluntarily elect ordinary VAT taxation. Intra-Community acquisitions, imports, exports, cross-border services, and transactions requiring a VAT number can trigger registration or reporting obligations independently of the domestic franchise thresholds. A manufacturer of intraocular lenses should generally register for VAT before taxable domestic sales, imports, or intra-Community transactions, regardless of reliance on the franchise regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for all domestic invoices. Invoices must comply with French VAT invoicing requirements and must be retained in an auditable electronic or documentary form. Electronic invoicing reform provides for mandatory receipt of electronic invoices by all businesses from 1 September 2026. Mandatory issuance is scheduled from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and certain intermediate-sized enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises, subject to statutory implementation rules and any approved postponements. Invoices will generally be transmitted through an approved private platform or the public invoicing platform architecture, with structured data reporting to the tax administration. E-reporting will cover specified business-to-consumer and international transactions. Public-sector invoices must be submitted through Chorus Pro. Digital signatures, qualified electronic seals, electronic data interchange, or reliable audit-trail controls may be used to establish authenticity, integrity, and legibility; France does not generally require a tax authority digital stamp before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT where the supplier establishes that the goods physically leave the EU and satisfies the French VAT and customs evidence requirements. The supplier must normally be the exporter or act through an authorized representative and must retain the export customs declaration, the electronic exit result or equivalent proof of exit, commercial invoices, transport evidence, and a transaction trail linking the goods to the export. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt from French VAT where the customer is identified for VAT in another EU Member State, the goods are transported from France to that Member State, and the supplier holds the required proof and submits the relevant recapitulative statement. Services are not automatically zero-rated. Business-to-business services are generally located where the customer is established, subject to special place-of-supply rules; supporting evidence of customer status, contractual scope, and place of performance is required. Exports of medical devices remain subject to product, customs, and regulatory compliance requirements in addition to VAT conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration, including the applicable export procedure and commodity classification
MRN and electronic exit confirmation or equivalent customs proof that the goods exited the European Union
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR, or courier manifest
Sales contract, purchase order, and accounting records linking the shipment to the invoice
Evidence of customs representation and export authorization where a customs broker or indirect representative is used
Proof of import or delivery in the destination country where reasonably available

Inward remittance evidence or bank records where relevant to commercial substantiation; France does not generally require a standardized inward remittance certificate as a condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days as a condition for French VAT zero-rating. Export VAT treatment depends primarily on proof of dispatch and exit from the European Union, not on a fixed foreign-exchange repatriation period. If export conditions are not proven, the tax administration may reassess French VAT, normally at the applicable rate, together with late-payment interest under the French Tax Code. Intentional or abusive conduct may attract an 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, or other applicable penalties under the French Tax Code; lesser penalties may apply for negligence or procedural failures. False customs declarations may trigger customs recovery, administrative fines, seizure, and criminal sanctions under the Union Customs Code and French customs law. Tax reassessment is generally subject to the ordinary VAT limitation period, commonly three years following the relevant tax year, subject to extension or special rules for fraud, concealed activity, or criminal proceedings. A manufacturer should retain export, customs, transport, customer, VAT, and accounting records for the statutory retention period and be able to reconcile each zero-rated invoice to the corresponding customs exit record.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating as the central bank of the French Republic within the European System of Central Banks and the Eurosystem; foreign-exchange, capital-movement and investment-screening control is administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the French Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; prudential supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic-money institutions is exercised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is unconditionally convertible for both current-account and capital-account operations. France applies the OECD Codes of Liberalisation and the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63-66 TFEU); there is no exchange-licensing, approval or foreign-currency rationing requirement applicable to an SAS manufacturing intraocular acrylic lenses. Profit remittance by the SAS to shareholders is legally unrestricted; dividends to an EU/EEA corporate parent holding at least 10% qualify for full relief under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU (zero withholding tax if directive conditions are satisfied), while distributions to non-EU corporate shareholders are subject to the domestic 25% withholding tax, which may be reduced or eliminated under the applicable double-tax treaty or the domestic 'participation exemption' framework when applicable. The only operative hurdles are corporate-law formalities (shareholder decision, audited accounts where statutory thresholds trigger a statutory auditor, registration of the distribution) and statistical reporting to Banque de France for transactions exceeding the balance-of-payments reporting threshold (EUR 50,000 per transaction or the aggregate direct investment reporting threshold). No exchange-control approval or prior consent of the Treasury is required for ordinary dividends, royalties, or trade payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has abolished export-proceeds surrender and mandatory conversion obligations. There is no statutory requirement to repatriate export receipts to France or to convert foreign currency into euro; proceeds may lawfully remain in a foreign-currency account (compte en devises) held with a French credit institution. Export receivables arising from the sale of intraocular lenses must, however, be collected within the payment terms negotiated in the underlying international sales contract; where no term is expressly agreed, French Commercial Code (Article L441-10, as amended by the Loi de modernisation de l'économie) implies payment within 30 days of performance, and the maximum statutory term for invoiced commercial transactions is 60 days. Each export transaction is captured through the French customs merchandise declarations (DEB/DES) which feed the balance-of-payments statistics maintained by Banque de France; separate BOP declarations are required where the transaction is a service or financial flow above the threshold. No percentage of export proceeds is required to be swapped or sold to the central bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary operating account, Low as the primary or sole treasury host. An ACPR-licensed or EU-passported electronic-money institution (EMI) such as Qonto, Shine, Aria or Manager.One can open a French IBAN for the SAS with fully remote KYC, process SEPA euro payments, vendor cards and payroll, and offer basic FX markups. Legal and operational constraints are material: (i) EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, open documentary collections, sponsor SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA USD/CHF settlements, or act as a participant in high-value clearing systems (T2/TARGET2); (ii) their cross-border correspondent network is indirect and typically limited to retail P2P corridors; (iii) Polish-style or other offshore non-EEA EMIs have no passporting rights into France and their use would expose the SAS to sanctions-compliance gaps and French AML enforcement risk as a breach of the Monétical and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, Articles L521-1 to L521-3). For a high-risk medical-device manufacturer (ISIC 3250) with non-EU shareholders, the EMI should be reduced to a sub-limit disbursement wallet for domestic travel and small vendor expenses, never the cash-concentration, LC, or FX-hedging rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: As a practical matter, a physical KYC interview at a French branch is mandatory for the ultimate beneficial owner and the SAS legal representative. French banks have adopted digital onboarding only for clean, domestically resident SMEs with low-risk profiles; a foreign-owned, high-risk medical-device manufacturing entity triggers the compliance duty to 'know the physical person' behind the vehicle. The bank will require: (i) in-person attendance at a branch, or at the bank's dedicated international-desks where a video-conference interview authenticated by an ANSSI-certified digital identity verification is accepted only if original travelling-paper documentation is countersigned by a notary or the local French embassy; (ii) the appointment-only review of the corporate documentation head by head against the original passports of all signatories and of every shareholder holding more than 25% of the SAS share capital; (iii) for non-resident shareholders resident outside the EU, apostilled or legalised corporate extracts, respectively under the Apostille Convention of 1961 or the bilateral legalisation route; and (iv) a possible document-or-site check by the bank's healthcare-sector retail, wholesale and professional-risk unit. Fully remote opening is not viable for this transaction profile in the current French enforcement environment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Untraceable or undocumented beneficial-ownership chain above 25% of share capital or voting rights in the SAS.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A comprehensive RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) filing acknowledgement from the commercial registry; a formal organisational chart tracing legal and natural persons to the ultimate individual; notarised passports of every UBO; a sworn declaration by the SAS president confirming the exact percentages and the economic ownership free of third-party nominees; plus the corporate share register (registre des mouvements de titres) updated to the date of the bank interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU shareholder jurisdiction appears on internal bank watchlists or poses elevated money-laundering and sanctions risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Parent company audited financial statements for the last three financial years; a recent tax-residence certificate issued by the foreign tax authority of the investor; an original bank reference-letter from the investor's principal bank specifying account relationship length and average balances; sworn source-of-wealth statement broken down by legal origin (business profits, dividends, real-estate disposals); and a group-structure organigram vouched by a recognised firm of counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk medical-device sector dealing in Class III intraocular lenses, requiring statutory authorisation and EU regulated-market conformity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU Declaration of Conformity issued under the Medical Device Regulation (EU) 2017/745; CE-marking certificate issued by a Notified Body; ISO 13485:2016 quality-management certificate for sterile and non-sterile medical devices; ANSM (Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé) registration/declaration as manufacturer or authorised representative; a copy of the EU Importer/Manufacturer registration for all EU Member States where products are placed on the market; and the technical documentation schedule if the bank requests the essential-requirements checklist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large early-stage capital injection into a newly incorporated SAS with a foreign treasury parent, presenting unusual transactional patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised original deed of incorporation (statuts) of the SAS; the shareholder capital-subscription resolution; the bank or notary certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de capital) proving the funds were blocked and released upon registration; the share-subscription payment instruction and its matching credit advice; the Kbis extract evidencing completed RCS registration; and forecast operating cash-flow projections demonstrating how the injected capital will fund raw-material purchasing for lens manufacturing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment routing or concentration-account structures that obscure the commercial counterparty behind the transaction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signatory-matrix and instruction mandate form listing all bank accounts of clients and suppliers in the first-year transaction schedule; signed master purchase or distribution agreements referencing the intraocular-lens trade; sample commercial invoice with Incoterms 2020; customs export/import declarations (DEB/DES or ENS) for the relevant shipment cycle; transport documents (B/L, AWB, CMR); FATCA and CRS self-certifications for the entity; and a written explanation of any concentration-account mechanics prepared by the corporate secretary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder's equity contribution shall be settled by SWIFT MT103 to the French SAS's dedicated bank account (IBAN FR76 and BIC of the Tier-1 bank), with remittance field 70 clearly stating: 'Souscription et versement du capital social – FR_SAS – facture de constitution'. The purpose codes embedded in the receiving bank's balance-of-payments processing must reflect 'equity investment / investment in share capital' (formation of direct-investment position). Before the wire, the SAS must complete the French corporate formalities: (i) shareholder resolution adopting the capital increase; (ii) deposit of funds with a French notary or bank (attestation de dépôt/blockage); (iii) publication of a legal notice in the Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) if required; (iv) filing of the constitutional documents with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce to obtain Kbis/INSEE registration; and (v) payment of the registration fee (droit d'enregistrement). If the subscriber is a non-EU shareholder, the transaction may constitute an inbound foreign direct investment under EU Regulation 452/2019 and French Decree No. 2019-1590 on the sensitive perimeter of 'santé' (health); prior sectoral screening by DG Trésor is required where the non-EU investor acquires 25% or more of the voting rights of the French entity, with a 10-working-day assessment period for prior authorisation and a 5-working-day period for non-objection. The routing instruction must be sent only after the bank's account-operations officer has confirmed receipt of the complete KYC/RBE file and the SHA/BEN charge-code has been set to avoid failed credit. Any capital inflow above EUR 50,000 must be reported in the France balance-of-payments statistics by the intermediary bank, without further action by the entity, in case the funds relate to the shareholders' current account while awaiting formal capital registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement is structured across three clearing rails. (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT, ISO 20022 pain.001) for euro payments to EU/EEA suppliers and distributors, executed directly in T2/TARGET2 with intraday finality, with a pragmatic cut-off discipline of D-1 for all forecast invoices; (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA and non-EUR payments (USD, CHF, GBP) to raw-material vendors of acrylic polymers, hydrophobic lens substrates, sterilisation consumables and packaging components, utilising the bank's foreign-correspondent network; and (3) commercial documentary instruments for high-value, first-transaction or moderately risky corridors: Irrevocable Letters of Credit issued under ICC UCP 600 (sight or 90-day deferred payment), Documentary Collections under URC 522 (D/P or D/A), Standby Letters of Credit under ISP98, and Bank Guarantees under URDG 758 for distribution agreements in the EU. All instructions must carry a fully populated payment-remittance reference block containing the invoice number, purchase-order number, Incoterms 2020 rule, and the HS/CN code (9003.11.00 for intraocular lens optical elements) to satisfy customs reconciliation. Each payment must be screened against EU financial-restrictive measures (asset-freezes, sectoral embargoes on medical devices) and the consolidated list ofthe European External Action Service before release; any suspicious-counterparty alert is resolved only after the bank's sanctions officer reviews the cleared documentary evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright deliverable forwards for the import of polymer raw materials denominated in USD

EUR/CNY and EUR/INR non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge Asian surgical-supply-chain exposures where deliverability is not available, subject to EMIR prudent-hedge documentation and the bank's credit-line approval
EUR/USD FX swaps for temporary liquidity conversion between the euro treasury and the USD trade account
Cross-currency interest-rate-swap agreements (EUR/USD) for medium-term alignment of the parent financing and trade payables
Plain-vanilla European call and put options on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF for premium-only protection against adverse exchange-rate movements
Rolling-spot FX facilities with monthly fixings, providing the treasury with continuation risk-management without or with the right to add forward dates
VanillaForward Rate Agreements (FRAs) and interest-rate swaps for managing the floating-rate leg of any import-financing line

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end; if closing on December 31, due by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal injunctive notice; court-imposed penalty (astreinte) up to 1,500 EUR; 5% late-payment penalty; risk of removal from RCS (forced strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats, form 2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day after May 1 for a December 31 close, typically May 3–4; extended to June 30 for online filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% penalty on unreported tax (10% if paid late); 0.20% monthly late-payment interest; additional penalties after 10-day formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Contribution foncière des entreprises (CFE) annual payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Interim instalment by June 15; final balance by December 15; no separate annual declaration if no changes in property
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% penalty on unpaid tax plus 1% monthly late-filing penalty; accrual of statutory interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner register update and filing upon shareholding changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following any change of beneficial ownership or within 30 days after any annual General Meeting approving share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to 7,500 EUR for individuals and 37,500 EUR for legal entities (French Monetary and Financial Code, Art. L561-5-2).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when, at year-end for two consecutive years, the entity exceeds at least two of the following: total balance sheet > 4,000,000 EUR; net turnover > 8,000,000 EUR; average employee count > 50. Smaller SAS may be exempt unless regulated; for a medical-device manufacturer not meeting these thresholds, an independent audit is voluntary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles (French GAAP, PCG) are compulsory for individual annual accounts; consolidated accounts may be prepared under French GAAP or IFRS if applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a standalone annual UBO declaration. The SAS must maintain a written register of beneficial owners at the registered office and file all changes with the Registry within 30 days of the transaction. Shareholding transfers are recorded in the register of securities (registre des mouvements de titres) and approved through written unanimous decisions unless otherwise provided in the articles; the annual confirmation of shareholding structure is incorporated in the annual accounts approval decision.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of securities and share transfers (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of decisions/minutes (registre des décisions de l'associé unique / procès-verbaux)
Register of beneficial owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first €42,500 of taxable income for SMEs under certain turnover thresholds; research tax credit (Créance d'Impôt Recherche - CIR) at 30% up to €100 million of eligible R&D expenditure, higher for certain collaborative research; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% up to €400,000 for SMEs; tax depreciation allowances (amortissements) and French territorial economic subsidies (e.g., innovation subsidies with tax-exempt status) may apply. Losses may generally be carried forward indefinitely, but annual offset is capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding that threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Liasse fiscale - CERFA 2065 plus core schedules (2052, 2058-SD, 2059-SD, 2065-SD) filed electronically via the EDI-TDFC (Échange de Données Informatisés - TéléDéclaration du Fichier Central des Comptes) portal operated by the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the third month following the fiscal year-end. For fiscal years ending 31 December via electronic filing, the return is due on the second business day after 1 May. For non-calendar fiscal years, the deadline is the same day as the third anniversary of the fiscal year-end; EDI filing grants a one-month extension in certain calendar-year cases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross French and foreign turnover (chiffre d'affaires) from sales of goods, including intraocular acrylic lenses, net of returns and rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report turnover actually generated in France; for intra-group sales to related French distributors, include sales at arm's length value and attach transfer pricing documentation if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 (2052 - Inventory variation and other operating income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Change in inventory (finished lens stock, semi-finished materials) and transfer of fixed assets or other operating revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident manufacturers with French permanent establishment (PE) must include cost allocations attributable to the PE under the OECD PE profit attribution standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 14 to 23 (2058-SD - Taxable income determination, DBA and DBR)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses, depreciation, provisions, professional costs, and foreign tax credits. Specific lines capture research tax credit (CIR) carry-forward offsets and tax-exempt subsidies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses economically linked to French source income are deductible. For intercompany royalties, withhold at source and substantiate beneficial ownership under the applicable treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2065-SD - Declaration of encashment and tax payment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax (IS) due after reconciliation of deductions and credits, including social contribution surcharge (Contribution Sociale sur les Bénéfices - CSB).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident companies taxed on a PE, the CSB applies to net profits attributable to the PE. Payment is made via VAT account 3349 or wire transfer with referenced SIREN number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of transactions with related parties or entities located in tax-privileged jurisdictions, including loans, royalties, and commission arrangements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities controlling a French SAS must provide official documentation proving arm's length conduct; failure triggers automatic reassessment under Article L.13 A of the French Tax Procedures Book.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge of tax payable plus 0.2% monthly late interest (intérêt de retard). If a formal notice is not satisfied, the surcharge increases to 20%; bad faith or fraudulent behavior raises the penalty to 40% or 80% respectively. Minimum penalties may apply for omitted schedules. Erroneous or incomplete transfer pricing documentation may also trigger a fixed €15,000 fine.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on gross dividends paid to non-resident companies; 30% for individuals (12.8% undistributed income tax plus 17.2% social levies) absent treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Claim reduced treaty rate (often 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on shareholding) by submitting French Form 5000 (residence certificate), Form 5001 (treatment certificate), and Form 5002 (authorization to obtain exchange of information) to the French tax authorities before cash distribution. The beneficial owner must be established under the relevant DTA. EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption applies where shareholding exceeds 10% and the holding period is at least two years; the payor must receive a current French tax residence certificate and an attestation of actual holding. Rejection or insufficient documentation: immediate withholding at full statutory rate and possible interest for late payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding tax (WHT) for IP royalties (patents, know-how, trademarks) paid to non-residents is 33.33% under Article 182 B CGI, reduced by treaty (commonly 0-10% for licensing contracts with substantive holding). Interest paid to non-residents is generally exempt from French WHT at source (0%) when the lender is not considered delinquent and the transaction is not routed through a non-cooperative state (treaty abuse). For payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions (blue list turquoise), WHT of 50% may apply to interest and 60% to royalties. French anti-abuse rules require economic substance and correct beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Master File and Local File are mandatory when the group consolidated revenue exceeds €400,000,000 or when the French entity's annual net turnover/balance sheet exceeds €400,000,000. Small and medium enterprises with less than €7,829,417 turnover are exempt from TP documentation, except when the taxpayer is a parent entity without French operations or where a tax haven benefit is concerned. The annual TP report under Article L.13 AA is required for entities within a group meeting the €400 million threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply the UAE ESR itself, but French tax law embodies the OECD substance criteria through Article 119 D (anti-abuse) and BEPS standards. For treaty relief, the beneficial owner concept and the 'Austrian' or 'AB' treaty shopping clauses require the recipient to conduct genuine economic activity. A French SAS with no real activity, no staff, no premises, or no operational risks may be deemed a 'conduit company' and its transactions re-characterized under Article 1655 A. For intraocular lens manufacturing, substantive activities include maintaining raw material and finished goods inventories, executing rapid priority surgical lens contracts, holding quality certifications (ISO 13485), and bearing production and product-liability risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to report French sales of intraocular lenses through an undisclosed permanent establishment; use of invoicing companies in tax havens with no real activity; false deduction of management fees or royalty treatments not corresponding to actual provision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A minimum of 50% increase to tax base under Article 1728 CGI (bad faith penalty); intentional concealment or disguised activity carries a 80% penalty; representation by an intermediary in a tax-haven jurisdiction may trigger a separate 2% penalty per payment. Financial penalties can reach 100% of undeclared tax where false document is used. Pecuniary and non-pecuniary penalties follow a criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to €75,000 (or increased for corporate liability under Article L. 271-1).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Direct exposure for unpaid taxes and social security under Article L.267 of the French Tax Procedures book (Livre des procédures fiscales) when deliberate behavior has made recovery impossible; travel bans (interdiction de sortie du territoire) may be ordered; debt recovery via garnishment of personal assets. Directors may also face criminal conviction for complicity in tax evasion under Articles 1746/1757 CGI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French SAS that holds only a mailbox or virtual office, no locally based executive decision-making, no independent stock levels, and delegates all manufacturing and removals to an affiliated non-resident parent, rendering the French entity an 'inset' without underlying economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment: disregarded entity status under the abuse of law procedure (abus de droit) under Article L.64 LPF. Re-characterization of the billing model results in full French tax leakage (25% IS plus VAT on outward supplies), penalties of 80% in cases of deliberate abuse, and non-deductibility of contractual transactions. Potential withdrawal of the free-practice license for intraocular lens distribution under the French Medical Device Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors (président, directeur général) personally liable for the added tax deficits if they knew or caused the transfer-pricing misstatement; they may face restitution orders in civil proceedings under Art. L.267; travel ban pending full settlement; if evidence of fraud in the commercial registration is present, criminal penalty of 3 years' imprisonment and €45,000 fine under Art. 441-5 Code pénal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving sales proceeds from intraocular lenses via high-risk payment rails when the beneficial owner is undisclosed; payment arrangement routed through third-party intermediaries with no apparent economic reason or due diligence; use of SWIFT wire transfers from shell financial institutions in countries with weak AML controls, failing to report suspicious transactions to TRACFIN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the French Monetary and Financial Code Articles 324-1 to 324-4, money laundering is punished by up to 10 years' imprisonment and fine of up to €750,000 for companies; business license revocation possible; confiscation of company assets ; commercial registration of the SAS cancelled by public prosecutor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and key compliance officers held criminally liable for having knowingly directed or participated in laundering. Discretionary imprisonment version up to 10 years when the infrastructure is intentional; permanent travel prohibition and ban from professional practice; civil liability toward third-party creditors for amounts laundered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Tax Return / Digital Tax Infringement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of the liasse fiscale in the EDI system after expiry of the deadline, or non-submission of the annual related-party transaction declaration (2069-SD) when required; non-payment of corporate tax instalments despite taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1728 CGI: 10% uplift on tax due for courteous default; 20% after a formal 30-day reminder; 40% in case of active bad faith; 80% for fraudulent concealment. Additionally, 0.2% monthly late-interest (intérêt de retard) accrues during the entire collection period. Fixed penalty of €150 for non-filing each of the supplementary schedules if deemed applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the 80% fraud penalty if they signed false declarations; administrative protection of the tax authority may impose garnishment restraint; under certain recurrent non-filing with intent to evade, criminal prosecution pursuant to Art. 1741 CGI applies, leading to 5 years imprisonment and €75,000 fine; further, deletion of the SIREN and ban from managing a company under commercial law for up to 15 years.
